Usage: gwt merged <target> ... [flags]

Judge whether branches or commits are merged into the trunk.

Prints whether each target's work is in the trunk, one line per judged target in
order: "merged<TAB><target>", or "unmerged<TAB><target>" when the trunk is not
confirmed to hold it. A full commit id, such as a detached checkout's HEAD, is
judged as that commit. Verdicts, unmerged ones included, exit 0. A target that
cannot be judged, such as a branch that does not exist, gets no line: it is
reported on stderr as "gwt: error: <target>: <reason>" (in JSON, by its error
field), the rest are still judged, and the command exits 1.

Without --fetch it contacts no remote. --into's revision must exist locally.

Arguments:
  <target> ...      Local branches, with or without a checkout, or full commit ids where no branch
                    has the name.

Flags:
      --fetch       First fetch a remote trunk that no fetch has reached within fetch.max_age, so a
                    merge made on the remote since counts.
      --into=REV    Judge against REV instead of the trunk, such as a base you verified against the
                    remote yourself; nothing is fetched.
      --json        Print one JSON object instead of lines.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help        Show context-sensitive help.

Constraints:
  At most one of --fetch, --into.

JSON:
  One object, printed even when a target cannot be judged; nothing when the trunk
  or the --into revision cannot be resolved (exit 1):
    trunk     what the verdicts were measured against, as gwt trunk --json prints
              it; with --into, its name and commit are that revision
    branches  one object per target, in order:
      branch  the target as given
      commit  the commit judged; absent when the target was not found
      merged  whether it is merged; null when not found or when the check failed
      error   why it could not be judged; absent otherwise

The trunk and merge verdicts:
  The trunk is where work lands: the first of origin/HEAD, origin/main,
  origin/master, main and master that exists, else the main checkout's branch. It
  is not create's base, which only says where a new branch forks from.

  A branch is merged into the trunk when the trunk contains its commits, when one
  trunk commit carries its combined change (a squash merge), or when trunk commits
  carry each of its commits' changes (a rebase). A change match also needs a clean
  merge that leaves the trunk's contents exactly as they are. A branch with merge
  commits of its own, or whose lines the trunk edited again later, may stay
  unconfirmed, which reads as unmerged. A branch with no commits of its own
  counts as merged: it holds nothing to lose.

  Verdicts read cached remote refs. A command that fetches first (--fetch, and
  remove) does so only when the last fetch gwt can see, the main checkout's
  FETCH_HEAD, is older than fetch.max_age, bounded by fetch.timeout; a failed fetch
  warns on stderr and the verdicts use the cached refs. To be sure a merge made
  moments ago counts, run git fetch yourself first.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed, or a creation was declined; also remove when any target failed, and merged when any
       target could not be judged, after printing every target's result
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
